did_you_know.text: Did you know? Chapter 6 presents the three main families of the tribe of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
Did you know? The chapter details the long genealogies of the Levite families, including the lines of Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
Did you know? The family line of Kohath includes Elkanah, Samuel, and his sons Joel and Abijah, highlighting the family connection between the Levites and Samuel.
Did you know? David appointed Levites to serve as singers in the house of the Lord; they sang before the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, and continued until the temple was built in Solomon’s time.
Did you know? Heman is described as a singer from the family of Kohath, and his genealogy extends back to Jacob, who is called Israel here.
Did you know? Alongside Heman, Asaph and Ethan are mentioned; they too were singers from the tribe of Levi, and the chapter also lists their genealogies.
Did you know? The Levites were assigned all the work of the tabernacle, the house of God, while Aaron and his sons were responsible for the altar, the incense, and making atonement for Israel.
Did you know? The priestly line in this chapter continues from Aaron through Eleazar and Phinehas to Ahimaaz.
Did you know? The descendants of Aaron were given cities within the territories of the tribes, including cities of refuge such as Hebron, Libnah, Jattir, and Eshtemoa.

Did you know? The Levitical cities were distributed among the families of Kohath, Gershon, and Merari from the territories of the tribes of Israel: the descendants of Kohath received ten cities, the descendants of Gershon thirteen, and the descendants of Merari twelve.
